defects.description: PRESENT: Look 2 still reads as smooth coated material with chalk-bright seam outlines, rather than the reference's worn black denim.
defects.evidence: S01@00:01.500 and S01@00:02.500 show broad smooth highlights and conspicuously pale stitching across the fronts and pocket edges.
defects.recommended_action: Regenerate the material treatment against the denim reference while preserving the source performance.

defects.description: PRESENT: hardware proportions and exaggerated pocket-flap edging remain product-inaccurate. The macro emphasizes the mismatch rather than establishing garment authenticity.
defects.evidence: S01@00:03.500 shows large pale fasteners; S02@00:04.500 enlarges the outlined flaps and buttons; S04@00:12.500 retains conspicuous hardware.
defects.recommended_action: Use one reference-matched hardware and pocket construction across performance renders and the macro.

defects.description: PRESENT: pre-hook cuts exchange jacket length, wear distribution and fastener treatment instead of maintaining one Look 2 garment.
defects.evidence: S01@00:03.500 has longer outlined fronts; S03@00:06.500 introduces a shorter, more washed body and cuffs; S04@00:12.500 changes the front hardware presentation again.
defects.recommended_action: Propagate one approved jacket construction across cuts, accounting for pose and S04's crop.

defects.description: PRESENT: the lower fronts separate beneath the zipper and expose pale underlying material. This is a lower-closure failure, not permitted shirt-and-tie visibility at the neck.
defects.evidence: S08@00:27.500 shows a triangular opening below the closure; S08@00:28.500 exposes a pale strip between the lower fronts.
defects.recommended_action: Restore the approved closed lower front and continuous zipper-to-hem construction.

defects.description: PRESENT under the documented nonblocking styling exception: tie, shirt and cuff variants persist. Approved neck-layer visibility is not classified as an open-jacket defect.
defects.evidence: S06@00:17.500 uses a fine-striped tie; S09@00:30.500 has ribbed mastic cuffs; S11@00:35.500 displays broad white cuffs.
defects.recommended_action: Retain the recorded exception; do not introduce an additional release block for these styling differences.

defects.description: PRESENT: unapproved body and pocket construction still prevents a consistent product realization. Accepted late-hook styling differences are not counted as an additional release block.
defects.evidence: S08@00:25.500 presents a long, comparatively flat front; S12@00:39.500 shows high angular pocket openings unlike the reference's lower slit-pocket construction.
defects.recommended_action: Use the approved realization as the shared body and pocket anchor, preserving documented styling tolerances.

defects.description: PRESENT: the city insert still separates visibly different Look 1 jacket bodies rather than concealing a continuous garment realization.
defects.evidence: S06@00:21.500 has a short gathered body and broad flared collar; S08@00:24.500 returns with straighter elongated fronts and a much smaller upright collar.
defects.recommended_action: Match S08's collar, body proportions and waistband to the approved hook anchor before propagation.

defects.description: PRESENT: waistband definition and lower-front geometry change across sampled arm-crossing and turning poses, independently of the remaining edge-mask damage.
defects.evidence: S08@00:25.500 has an irregular central termination; S08@00:26.500 develops unequal lower fronts; S08@00:27.500 restores a more defined band around an open central split.
defects.recommended_action: Propagate a single pose-aware waistband and closure model throughout S08.

defects.description: PRESENT within accepted late-hook tolerance: cross-cut garment variants remain visible but are not independently release-blocking.
defects.evidence: S09@00:30.500 has a continuous pale ribbed hem; S11@00:35.500 uses separated white waistband sections; S12@00:39.500 returns to a mastic waistband.
defects.recommended_action: Track the variance without expanding the exception to cover defective band or matte integration.

defects.description: PRESENT: the wearer-right chest stripe loses sections to beige wedges instead of remaining a complete band that follows the garment.
defects.evidence: S11@00:35.500 shows a rectangular stripe segment; S11@00:36.500 introduces a diagonal beige interruption; S11@00:37.500 leaves the wearer-right segment visibly truncated.
defects.recommended_action: Track a complete stripe through garment deformation and preserve its continuity under folds.

defects.description: PRESENT: the replacement band reads as a graphic overlay, with hard patch boundaries and implausible integration around the neck-layer opening.
defects.evidence: S11@00:33.500 exposes an abrupt horizontal patch around the tie opening; S11@00:35.500 shows squared ends and mismatched stripe levels beside the neck layer.
defects.recommended_action: Rebuild garment-surface warping, shading and neck-layer occlusion; do not solve this by enlarging the stripe.

defects.description: PRESENT: smoothing has not produced a consistently finished fabric boundary. Angular bites and pale remnants remain along the repaired lower edge.
defects.evidence: S08@00:25.500 retains pale central fringe; S08@00:26.500 has an abrupt lower-edge step; S08@00:28.500 shows a notched edge and pale residue near the split.
defects.recommended_action: Reconstruct the fabric silhouette and underlying occlusion rather than applying further edge smoothing alone.

defects.description: PRESENT: the moving wearer-right shoulder/upper-arm silhouette remains eroded into a stepped cutout.
defects.evidence: S06@00:21.500 shows a squared recess on the screen-left upper arm above the raised hand. S06@00:20.500 supplies the preceding extended-arm contour.
defects.recommended_action: Recover the missing sleeve silhouette from the source-aligned garment render and rebuild the motion-aware alpha.

defects.description: NEW: regenerated S06 satisfies the mastic exterior but exposes tan inward-facing collar surfaces instead of the required navy interior.
defects.evidence: S06@00:17.500 and S06@00:18.500 show broad tan inner collar faces with dark edging only; S09@00:30.500 provides a visibly dark interior comparison.
defects.recommended_action: Constrain the collar's separate inner and outer surfaces: navy inward, mastic outward, retaining approved neck styling.

overall.summary: The real-performance spine and cold-room progression survive, but garment truth and exposed repair seams prevent finished designer-commercial credibility. All 13 prior defects remain PRESENT; resolved IDs: none. S09 sleeve cleanup passes its sampled checkpoint. Scores cover the 43 supplied stills and exclude native timing, cadence and upscale quality.

answers.evidence: S01@00:02.500, S06@00:19.500 and S12@00:41.500 retain the anchor's recognizable face, beard, glasses and cap. Confidence 0.9 for sampled recognizability.
answers.question: 1. Does Fendi remain recognizably the same real person throughout the performance shots?
answers.answer: Yes at the sampled instants. No visible alternate performer replaces him. This establishes recognizable identity, not frame-for-frame preservation of every source expression or pose.

answers.evidence: S03@00:08.500 shows sleeve/hand interaction; S06@00:16.500 carries clothing through crossed arms; S08@00:27.500 exposes the defective lower closure.
answers.question: 2. Is the YSL / Saint Laurent wardrobe actually and convincingly worn by Fendi?
answers.answer: It is visibly on his body, not merely adjacent product imagery. Convincing wear is inconsistent: material inaccuracies, construction changes and exposed patching undermine the claim that these are the specified physical garments.

answers.evidence: S01@00:03.500 versus S03@00:06.500 establishes a cut-level reset; S08@00:28.500 shows unresolved construction during a torso turn.
answers.question: 3. Does the wardrobe remain stable during movement?
answers.answer: No. Sampled poses and cuts expose changing garment construction, particularly S08's lower fronts and S11's chest band. This finding concerns visible state changes, not unobserved inter-frame shimmer or flicker.

answers.evidence: S11@00:36.500 has a stripe interruption. S06@00:21.500 needs an unscaled crop to distinguish a possible ghost mark from shading. S09@00:30.500 provides the clean placement checkpoint.
answers.question: 4. Where exactly does the wordmark/logo break?
answers.answer: The confirmed failure is S11's supporting band, not readable spelling. S06's final sampled mark may have a faint duplicate: UNCERTAIN, confidence 0.3. S09 shows one small wearer-left mark confined to navy, without demonstrated beige spill. Exact lettering is excluded.

answers.evidence: S11@00:35.500 and S12@00:39.500–00:42.500 keep the visible mark small relative to its chest-band segment. Confidence 0.85 for absence of obvious oversizing.
answers.question: 5. Is any lettering visibly oversized or mis-scaled relative to the reference, especially S11 and S12?
answers.answer: No obvious oversizing is visible in S11 or S12. Their marks remain subordinate to the band. S11's objection is band construction and integration, not an oversized wordmark.

answers.evidence: S06@00:18.500 exposes tan inner collar surfaces; S09@00:30.500 shows plain mastic sleeves and ribbed cuffs without an obvious foreign badge or pale edge island.
answers.question: 6. Are there other garment defects, and did the targeted S09 sleeve cleanup work?
answers.answer: The regenerated S06 collar still violates the binding facing-color requirement. S09's sleeve cleanup passes the available visual checkpoint, but one sample cannot certify the entire shot. Accepted shirt/tie visibility is not being relabeled as a defect.

answers.evidence: Confidence 0.1. S11@00:35.500 and S12@00:40.500 are reduced samples, not matched native source/render crops. Compare synchronized master and export frames at delivery resolution without rescaling.
answers.question: 7. Does the native-resolution transformation/upscale visibly hurt quality relative to the source contact sheet?
answers.answer: UNVERIFIABLE FROM SAMPLES

answers.evidence: S01@00:01.500 replaces the closet with charcoal walls and one tall panel; S06@00:16.500 and S12@00:42.500 retain the expanded reflective room without shelves or hanging clothes.
answers.question: 8. Does the environment composite convincingly eliminate the original closet?
answers.answer: Yes at the sampled instants. The white door, shelves and hanging clothes no longer read. The single-panel pre-hook room and multiplied cold hook environment form an intentional progression; performer-edge defects are separate.

answers.evidence: S06@00:21.500 loses part of the raised-arm outline; S08@00:25.500 and S08@00:28.500 retain unfinished lower-boundary remnants.
answers.question: 9. Do matte/composite boundaries remain believable during movement?
answers.answer: Not consistently. The targeted shoulder and hem repairs still expose the composite. These are visible silhouette/occlusion failures, not merely a subjective preference for softer or harder edges.

answers.evidence: S02@00:04.500 supplies hardware detail; S05@00:15.500 supplies diamond refraction; S07@00:22.500 supplies cold rainy-city imagery.
answers.question: 10. Does B-roll feel intentional and compatible with the treatment?
answers.answer: Yes in purpose, but not uniformly in execution. The macro supports fashion language while magnifying inaccurate product details. Diamond, night-city and corridor imagery maintain the ice/luxury vocabulary without introducing an identifiable substitute performer.

answers.evidence: S06@00:16.500 establishes the expanded mirror room; S10@00:32.500 displays tonal inversion; S11@00:33.500 contains a pale return-transition state.
answers.question: 11. Do transitions work visually at the sampled instants?
answers.answer: The sampled changes are legible and compatible with the cold-world escalation. Visible FX states support the intended edit grammar, but they do not establish the complete flash, strobe or glitch behavior.

answers.evidence: Confidence 0.1. S05@00:15.500 and S11@00:33.500 cannot establish beat placement; S12@00:42.500 precedes the out. Check native video with audio against the song clock and final-hit waveform.
answers.question: 11a. Are cuts, flash, strobe and hard out musically aligned?
answers.answer: UNVERIFIABLE FROM SAMPLES

answers.evidence: Confidence 0.2. S05@00:15.500, S10@00:32.500 and S11@00:33.500 capture isolated states. Inspect every native frame through S05/S06 and S10/S11 to measure whiteout, strobe cadence and glitch duration.
answers.question: 11b. Can flash, strobe, glitch duration or sub-sample flicker be verified?
answers.answer: UNVERIFIABLE FROM SAMPLES

answers.evidence: S03@00:06.500, S08@00:24.500 and S11@00:33.500 visibly restore performance content in their designated post-insert slots.
answers.question: 12. Does the edit visibly return to the performer in the intended slots after B-roll/FX?
answers.answer: Yes. S03, S06, S08 and S11 return to Fendi after their inserts, and S09 contains the crossed-arm performance slot. This confirms content ordering, not native cut-boundary accuracy.

answers.evidence: Confidence 0.1. S09@00:30.500 demonstrates pose only. Verify native presentation timestamps, source-frame mapping and lip/gesture alignment against audio, especially insert returns and S09's different source in-point.
answers.question: 12a. Are source ranges, cut boundaries and audio/lip/gesture synchronization accurate within one native frame?
answers.answer: UNVERIFIABLE FROM SAMPLES

answers.evidence: S02@00:04.500 exposes product-detail inaccuracies; S08@00:27.500 fails lower closure; S11@00:36.500 fails the chest-band gate.
answers.question: 13. Does every shot substantially conform to its ShotSpec?
answers.answer: No. The intended performance/insertion structure and environment strategy are recognizable, but multiple performance shots fail garment and compositing requirements. The following grouped checks separate content conformance from technical failures.

answers.evidence: S01@00:01.500 establishes the room; S03@00:07.500 retains expressive hand work; S04@00:12.500 is visibly tighter. Exact source-relative crop/push factors remain UNCERTAIN, confidence 0.3.
answers.question: 13a. ShotSpec checks: S01, S03 and S04.
answers.answer: Partial conformance. Real performance, cold single-panel staging and S04's framing escalation survive. Denim fidelity and cross-cut garment continuity fail. A matched source comparison is needed to measure the specified push and crop factors.

answers.evidence: S02@00:04.500 and S02@00:05.500 frame the chest hardware and seams without a visible face.
answers.question: 13b. ShotSpec check: S02.
answers.answer: Partial conformance. The hardware closeup provides the requested fashion punctuation, but its buttons, flap edging and material treatment are not product-true. No facial performance appears in the insert.

answers.evidence: S05@00:15.500 shows the refracting diamond; S07@00:22.500 shows the wet night-city view; S10@00:32.500 shows an inverted multiplied corridor.
answers.question: 13c. ShotSpec checks: S05, S07 and S10.
answers.answer: Their visible subject matter substantially conforms. The inserts reinforce diamond, luxury-night and mirror-multiplication motifs. Required last-beat whiteout and temporal FX behavior remain governed by the native-media checks above.

answers.evidence: S06@00:21.500 exposes the shoulder defect; S08@00:26.500 exposes lower-front instability; S09@00:30.500 contains crossed arms, a dark collar interior and clean visible sleeves.
answers.question: 13d. ShotSpec checks: S06, S08 and S09.
answers.answer: Partial conformance. Look 1 and the hardened multi-mirror setting occupy the intended performance slots. S06's collar/matte and S08's construction remain defective. S09's pose and sleeve cleanup read correctly, without establishing one consistent garment across these shots.

answers.evidence: S11@00:36.500 has the fragmented stripe; S12@00:39.500 presents another pocket/body configuration; S12@00:42.500 still retains the recognizable performer and hook room.
answers.question: 13e. ShotSpec checks: S11 and S12.
answers.answer: Partial conformance. Direct performance and environmental continuity survive. S11's band integration fails objectively; S12 retains product-construction variance. The sampled ending does not certify the requested hard-out timing.

answers.evidence: S01@00:02.500 establishes the dark look; S06@00:18.500 supplies the pale hook contrast; S08@00:28.500 exposes the unfinished garment boundary.
answers.question: 14. Does the complete sequence resemble the intended luxury fashion commercial x contemporary rap treatment?
answers.answer: Recognizably, but it falls short of designer-commercial finish. Two contrasting looks and the mirror/ice world preserve the treatment. Inaccurate products and conspicuous repairs make parts of the fashion presentation look synthesized. Musical energy cannot be established from silent stills.

answers.evidence: S03@00:07.500 is driven by Fendi's expression and gesture; S08@00:28.500 reveals hem damage; S11@00:36.500 exposes the artificial stripe repair.
answers.question: 15. Does this look like a REAL Fendi video enhanced by AVT, or AI content built around his song?
answers.answer: Closer to a real Fendi video enhanced by AVT: his face and gestures remain the organizing performance, with subordinate inserts. Nevertheless, the broken hem and pasted stripe expose the AI construction and prevent this from reading as a finished, convincing fashion film.

answers.evidence: S06@00:18.500 has tan inner collar faces; S09@00:30.500 has a dark interior and ribbed trim; S11@00:36.500 combines stripe interruption with white cuffs and waistband sections.
answers.question: 16. Does the hook look read as ONE garment across S06/S08/S09/S11/S12, and which shot deviates most?
answers.answer: No. Shared mastic/navy colors unify the idea, not the construction. S11 deviates most through its incomplete graphic band and white trim. S09 improves collar-facing fidelity, but the differing collars, bodies, sleeves and waist treatments still prevent a single continuous product.
